narrationScript: For your next hands-on challenge, you'll complete the implementations for Selection Sort and Insertion Sort, following the logic we discussed earlier. Once all three sorting functions are ready, create a `main` function to put them to the test. Declare an initial unsorted array, then create three *identical copies* of this array. This is crucial for fair comparison. Call each sorting function on a separate copy, and after each sort, print the original array and the resulting sorted array. This will visually confirm their correctness. As an optional but highly recommended challenge, modify each sort function to include counters for swaps and comparisons. Printing these counts for different initial array states will provide a concrete, empirical understanding of their efficiency differences and how Big O notation manifests in practice. This activity will solidify your understanding of how these algorithms function and perform.
speakingStyle: A clear, confident, and enthusiastic tone, suitable for technical instruction.
deliveryNotes: Explain the purpose of printing results
